topic: Strange borders countdown: Chung Ying Street and India's nested enclave
hook: Your street can be half Hong Kong and half China, and India has an even stranger border.
title: 6 Strange Borders, India's Is the Wildest
description:
Six real borders that make no sense: a Spanish town inside France, a US peninsula you reach through Canada, a road across an airport runway, a German town using Swiss money, a street split between Hong Kong and China, and India's nested enclave in Cooch Behar. Every one is true, and every one is on a real map. Watch to the end for the strangest border of all.

#borders #geography #facts

scenes.narration: Your street can be half Hong Kong and half China, and India has an even stranger border.
scenes.headline: Streets Split By Borders

scenes.narration: By the end of this video, you will see a farm plot in India that sat inside a pocket, inside a pocket, inside a pocket.
scenes.headline: A Field Inside Fields

scenes.narration: Six real borders, each one stranger than the last. Every one of them is on a real map, and you can check them yourself.
scenes.headline: Six Real Borders

scenes.narration: The last two are the best, and the very last one is in India. Stay with me, because it gets weird fast.
scenes.headline: India Comes Last

scenes.narration: We start small, with a quiet mountain town where a very old mistake in a treaty still decides who owns the land.
scenes.headline: An Old Mistake

scenes.narration: So here is number six: a Spanish town that France completely surrounds, and the odd reason it is still Spanish.
scenes.headline: Border Number Six

scenes.narration: Number six. Llívia is a Spanish town, but you will not find it on the Spanish side of the mountains.
scenes.headline: Llívia

scenes.narration: It sits inside France, a short drive from the border. Spanish flags fly there, and people live by Spanish rules.
scenes.headline: Spanish Inside France

scenes.narration: The reason goes back to 1659. In a peace treaty, Spain agreed to hand a group of villages over to France.
scenes.headline: The 1659 Treaty

scenes.narration: But Llívia was counted as a town, not a village. So by the wording of the treaty, it was never given away.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: Think about that. One word in an old document, and hundreds of years later the map still shows a Spanish island in France.
scenes.headline: One Word Did It

scenes.narration: Today a special road links Llívia to the rest of Spain. That road is treated as neutral ground between the two countries.
scenes.headline: The Neutral Road

scenes.narration: So you can drive from Spain to this Spanish town while the French countryside rolls past on both sides of your window.
scenes.headline: Spain Through France

scenes.narration: It also has a pretty old centre and a church on a hill, and the views over the French hills are lovely.
scenes.headline: A Town On A Hill

scenes.narration: A town that is Spanish on paper and French on every side, all because a treaty forgot one place.
scenes.headline: Forgotten By A Treaty

scenes.narration: That is strange, but at least you can drive there. The next place has a road you must leave your own country to use.
scenes.headline: Strange, But Wait

scenes.narration: Let us go from Europe to the west coast of North America, where one border line cut right through a peninsula.
scenes.headline: To The Pacific Coast

scenes.narration: Number five. Point Roberts is part of the United States, in the state of Washington, and the map shows it clearly.
scenes.headline: Point Roberts

scenes.narration: But the border was drawn along a straight line of latitude, the 49th parallel, and it sliced the tip of a peninsula off.
scenes.headline: A Straight Line

scenes.narration: That left a small piece of America that hangs below Canada, with no American road connecting it to the rest of the country.
scenes.headline: America, Cut Off

scenes.narration: So the only land route from Point Roberts to the rest of the United States goes through Canada.
scenes.headline: Through Canada

scenes.narration: Residents cross into Canada, drive through it, and then cross back into America. That is two border checks just to reach the next big town.
scenes.headline: Two Checks

scenes.narration: Or they can take a boat across the water, which skips Canada altogether, though the weather has to be kind.
scenes.headline: Or Take A Boat

scenes.narration: Imagine driving to the supermarket and needing to show your passport twice. For these people, that is normal life.
scenes.headline: Passport For Groceries

scenes.narration: It is still part of the United States, with American addresses, American laws and a very strange commute.
scenes.headline: Still America

scenes.narration: One straight line drawn on a map, long ago, and a whole community still pays for it every time it leaves home.
scenes.headline: A Line Drawn Long Ago

scenes.narration: But the next border does something even odder. It makes cars and people wait for airplanes.
scenes.headline: Cars Wait For Planes

scenes.narration: Now we go back to Europe, to a huge rock beside the sea, at the very south of Spain.
scenes.headline: A Rock By The Sea

scenes.narration: Number four. Gibraltar sits at the tip of Spain, and it belongs to the United Kingdom.
scenes.headline: Gibraltar

scenes.narration: The main road in from Spain crosses the airport runway. Yes, the very runway where aircraft land.
scenes.headline: Road Over Runway

scenes.narration: The road is called Winston Churchill Avenue, and for most of the day it is just a busy road.
scenes.headline: Winston Churchill Avenue

scenes.narration: But when a plane is about to land or take off, barriers come down and the cars and walkers all have to wait.
scenes.headline: Barriers Come Down

scenes.narration: Then the plane rolls across, the barriers lift, and people carry on to work, to school or to the beach.
scenes.headline: Then Life Continues

scenes.narration: So here the border between Spain and the UK is a place where you queue twice: once for the passport check, and again for a plane.
scenes.headline: Wait For A Plane

scenes.narration: And it all sits under a giant rock, with a small town built at its foot and monkeys running around on top.
scenes.headline: A Rock With Monkeys

scenes.narration: Very few borders in the world are crossed over a runway, and this is the one most people have heard about.
scenes.headline: A Runway Border

scenes.narration: The next place is not an island or a peninsula. It is a whole town that sits in the wrong country.
scenes.headline: A Town In The Wrong Place

scenes.narration: And the people there handle their money in a way that does not match the country they officially belong to.
scenes.headline: Odd Money

scenes.narration: Number three. Büsingen am Hochrhein is a German town, but Switzerland surrounds it on every side.
scenes.headline: Büsingen

scenes.narration: To drive from Büsingen to the rest of Germany, you have to pass through Swiss land. There is no way around.
scenes.headline: Swiss On All Sides

scenes.narration: The town is also part of the Swiss customs area, and the Swiss franc is used in everyday life there.
scenes.headline: Swiss Customs Area

scenes.narration: So it is a town with German law, a German address and Swiss money in the shops. Few places mix two countries so completely.
scenes.headline: Two Countries At Once

scenes.narration: If you enjoy strange places and facts like these, subscribe, because the next two borders are the best ones in the video.
scenes.headline: Subscribe For More

scenes.narration: These first four were odd, but you could still tell where the line was. The next one runs right down the middle of a street.
scenes.headline: A Line Down The Street

scenes.narration: Chung Ying Street is the heart of this next story, and it sits in a small town on the edge of Hong Kong.
scenes.headline: On The Edge Of Hong Kong

scenes.narration: Number two. Sha Tau Kok sits right next to the mainland Chinese city of Shenzhen, and a border cuts through the old town.
scenes.headline: Sha Tau Kok

scenes.narration: The name Chung Ying Street means China-Britain Street, and that name is no accident, because both countries met on this very road.
scenes.headline: China-Britain Street

scenes.narration: In 1898, Britain and China agreed on a border for the Hong Kong area. In this town, the line ran down the middle of the lane.
scenes.headline: The 1898 Line

scenes.narration: Stone markers were set into the road to show where the line goes. They are still there, numbered one after another.
scenes.headline: Stone Markers

scenes.narration: One side of a stone reads Anglo-Chinese Boundary 1898 in English. The other side carries Chinese writing for the same line.
scenes.headline: Two Languages

scenes.narration: So on one side of the street you are in Hong Kong, and on the other side you are in mainland China.
scenes.headline: One Street, Two Sides

scenes.narration: Shop doors face each other across the lane. Take a few steps across the road, and you are under a different system of laws.
scenes.headline: Shops Face Shops

scenes.narration: For many years the Hong Kong side lay inside a closed frontier zone, so even getting to the street needed a permit.
scenes.headline: A Permit To Enter

scenes.narration: That is why some people say it is the street with one road and two systems. The border is literally under your feet.
scenes.headline: Border Under Your Feet

scenes.narration: There is no wall down the middle, no fence, just old stones and a road that people have shared for over a century.
scenes.headline: No Wall, Just Stones

scenes.narration: A single lane, two governments, and a line that was drawn when the town was a fishing village.
scenes.headline: A Fishing Village Line

scenes.narration: Walk it slowly, and you cross a border without any gate, any guard or any sign other than a worn stone.
scenes.headline: Cross Without A Gate

scenes.narration: Strange, right? And yet it is still not the strangest border in this video. That one is in India.
scenes.headline: Not The Strangest

scenes.narration: To find it, we go to the far north of West Bengal, to a district called Cooch Behar, right on the border.
scenes.headline: Cooch Behar

scenes.narration: Number one. Here, India and Bangladesh once had a tangle of tiny pockets of land inside each other's territory.
scenes.headline: Pockets Of Land

scenes.narration: Over a hundred Indian pockets lay inside Bangladesh, and about fifty Bangladeshi pockets lay inside India.
scenes.headline: Pockets Everywhere

scenes.narration: They came from old deals between local kings, and then Partition in 1947 locked every one of them in place.
scenes.headline: Old Deals, Then 1947

scenes.narration: People who lived in these pockets were cut off from their own country. Many struggled to get schools, clinics, power and water.
scenes.headline: Cut Off From Home

scenes.narration: To reach your own country, you first had to cross foreign land. Sometimes you had to do it more than once.
scenes.headline: Foreign Land Around You

scenes.narration: Now for the part I promised. Among these pockets was a plot called Dahala Khagrabari, and it was the strangest of all.
scenes.headline: Dahala Khagrabari

scenes.narration: It was a piece of India, inside a piece of Bangladesh, inside a piece of India, inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Four Layers Deep

scenes.narration: That makes it the only third-order enclave in the world, a pocket inside a pocket inside a pocket, with nothing else like it.
scenes.headline: The Only One

scenes.narration: The plot was farmland with nobody living on it. Its owner was a Bangladeshi farmer who lived in the pocket around it.
scenes.headline: A Lonely Farm Plot

scenes.narration: So an Indian field was owned by a Bangladeshi farmer, who lived on Indian land, inside Bangladesh. Try drawing that on paper.
scenes.headline: Try Drawing It

scenes.narration: In 2015, India and Bangladesh finally swapped these pockets. India even changed its constitution to make it happen.
scenes.headline: The 2015 Swap

scenes.narration: Dahala Khagrabari went to Bangladesh on the first of August 2015, and the strangest plot on the map disappeared.
scenes.headline: Gone In August 2015

scenes.narration: People in the pockets could choose their country, and many finally got proper addresses, roads and electricity.
scenes.headline: A Real Address

scenes.narration: So the next time a border looks like a simple line on your phone, remember these six places.
scenes.headline: Simple Lines Lie

scenes.narration: A Spanish town in France, a US peninsula you reach through Canada, and a road that crosses a runway.
scenes.headline: The First Three

scenes.narration: A German town using Swiss money, a street split down the middle, and a field inside three other pockets of land.
scenes.headline: The Last Three

scenes.narration: Borders are drawn by people, and people make odd choices. And yes, your street really can be half Hong Kong and half China.
scenes.headline: Half Hong Kong, Half China

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: the country with no border at its own front door.
scenes.headline: Next Video
